newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profiles of Japanese firms in payoff scandal.
newsitem.headline: Profiles of Japanese firms in payoff scandal.

text.p: The following are brief profiles of Nomura Securities, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank and Yamaichi Securities, all implicated in the racketeer payoff scandal:
Nomura Securities Co Ltd:
FOUNDED: As a money-changing company in 1872

BACKGROUND: Incorporated in 1925 as the Osaka Nomura Bank, the firm grew to become the world's largest securities firm. But it has been no stranger to scandal, becoming involved in another payoffs scheme in 1991. Analysts have said that, because of Nomura's size, the government would be careful not to push the firm into extinction despite its admittedly illegal activities.
LATEST CURRENT PROFITS: 165 trillion yen ($1.40 billion) in the fiscal year ended in March.
EMPLOYEES: 9,938
HEADQUARTERS: Tokyo
Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd:
FOUNDED: In 1971 through the merger of Dai-Ichi Bank and Nippon Kangyo Bank.

BACKGROUND: Japan's third-largest bank in terms of assets, it has played a key role in the "Sankinkai" group of companies of interwoven alliances, which include other major firms such as Itochu Corp and Kobe Steel Ltd.
Industry analysts say the merger had created lingering problems with a system of alternate reshuffling of top managers from the two former companies.
It is also active in the U.S. financial futures market with a subsidiary in Chicago, where the futures are traded.
Like other banks it has been struggling in the post-bubble economy, having recorded its highest profits in 1989.
LATEST CURRENT PROFITS: Lost 349.90 trillion yen ($2.97 billion) in the fiscal year ended in March.
EMPLOYEES: 17,425
HEADQUARTERS: Tokyo
Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd:
FOUNDED: Company origins date back to 1897.
BACKGROUND: Company began as a private stockbroking firm in Tokyo and is the oldest of the "Big Four" of Japanese finance, but is also considered financially the weakest of the group.
It came close to failure in 1965 and was rescued through a bailout package. It has close ties with Fuji Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan.
LATEST CURRENT PROFITS: Lost 5.04 billion yen ($42.7 million) in the fiscal year ended in March.
EMPLOYEES: 7,332
HEADQUARTERS: Tokyo
